title: Jeep Grand Cherokee Engines by Year
description: Every factory engine in the Jeep Grand Cherokee by year, 1993–2026: the 4.0 six, Magnum, PowerTech and Hemi V8s, the SRT8, Trackhawk and 4xe.
intro: The Grand Cherokee arrived for 1993 and has been built in five generations: the ZJ, WJ, WK, WK2 and WL. The three-row Grand Cherokee L joined the WL range for 2021.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.

generations.name: ZJ
intro: The ZJ offered the 4.0 six and the 5.2 V8, then the 5.9 V8 in the 1998 5.9 Limited.

generations.name: WJ
intro: The WJ kept the 4.0 six and added the 4.7 PowerTech V8, with a high-output 4.7 from 2002.

generations.name: WK
intro: The WK brought the 3.7 V6, the 5.7 Hemi and, from 2006, the 6.1 Hemi of the SRT8. A Mercedes-built 3.0 turbodiesel was offered for 2007–2008.

generations.name: WK2
intro: The WK2 used the 3.6 Pentastar V6, the 5.7 Hemi, the 6.4 Hemi of the SRT8 and SRT, a 3.0 EcoDiesel, and in the 2018–2021 Trackhawk the supercharged 6.2 Hellcat V8. A WK2-based Grand Cherokee WK was sold alongside the new model for 2022.

generations.name: WL
intro: The WL offers the 3.6 V6, the 5.7 Hemi through 2024, the 4xe plug-in hybrid for 2022–2025 and, from 2026, the Hurricane 2.0 turbo four.

method: Every engine and year listed here was confirmed by at least three independent sources: the NHRA Stock Car Classification Guides, factory material such as GM Heritage Center information kits and sales brochures, EPA records and established references. Several Wikipedia articles count as one source. Where sources give different ratings, the factory figure is shown and the difference is noted. Factory race-only packages need two sources.
